title.narrative: Beyond pipes and toilets: Promoting the human rights to water and sanitation

description.narrative:
Improve the progressive realization of the human rights to safe drinking water and sanitation for all.

Specific Objective 1 ¿ Increased global, regional, and national advocacy to elevate political prioritization of the human rights to water and sanitation as a universal priority integral to achieving the SDGs ¿ SWA leads.

Specific Objective 2 ¿ Improved multi-sectoral and multi-stakeholder spaces platforms with an active participation of, inter alia, civil society and private sector, research institutions, UN agencies and donors to accelerate the coordinated delivery of and accountability for high-impact water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) activities ¿ SWA leads.

Specific Objective 3 ¿ Improved water and sanitation's centrality in climate action, policy and financing ¿ UNICEF leads.

Specific Objective 4 ¿ Improved inequalities and rights-based monitoring systems and use of data for better understanding of water and sanitation systems and dynamics at play ¿ UNICEF leads.

description.narrative: The Proportion of population using safely managed sanitation services, including a handwashing facility with soap and water is currently being measured by the proportion of the population using a basic sanitation facility which is not shared with other households and where excreta is safely disposed in situ or treated offsite. `Improved sanitation facilities include: flush or pour flush toilets to sewer systems, septic tanks or pit latrines, ventilated improved pit latrines, pit latrines with a slab, and composting toilets.
